description:
**The usage ledger is plumbed end to end and returns null for the provider chief runs by default.**

`_parse_usage()` (`engine/agent.sh` ~l.816) was written to read exactly the `{"type":"result","total_cost_usd":…,"usage":{…}}` line that `claude --output-format json` prints. The dispatch case at `engine/agent.sh:1094` runs `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --print` — **without `--output-format json`** — so that line never appears and every `agent.turn` event carries `usage: null`. `docs/reference/events.md` documents the outcome as expected behaviour: *"Expect `usage: null` on a default install."*

Two halves of chief were built to fit each other and are not connected. The consequence is that the event stream's usage contract — the runner-side data source for chief-cloud's `82-run-history-analytics-and-cost-persistence`, which is merged — is **vacuous for the default provider**. A spend ledger over claude runs has nothing to persist.

⚠️ **This is not a one-flag change, and the risk is the reason it has not happened.** Chief pipes the provider's stdout, tees it, and the agent loop READS that text — completion promises, progress, refusals. Asking for JSON changes the shape of the thing the loop parses. The turn's human-readable output must still reach the log and the loop unchanged; only the usage figures are new. A change that makes the ledger work by breaking completion detection is strictly worse than `null`.

⚠️ **`test/provider-conformance.sh` asserts the EXACT argv the engine composes for each provider**, from the `ROSTER` array near the top of that file. Changing claude's dispatch without updating that line is a red build — which is the harness working, not an obstacle.

userStories.title: A claude turn emits real usage figures
userStories.description: Ask claude for the structured result and feed it to the parser that already knows the shape.
acceptanceCriteria: An `agent.turn` event from a claude run carries non-null `input_tokens`, `output_tokens` and `cost_usd`.
`_parse_usage()` is REUSED, not rewritten — it already handles this exact shape.
The `ROSTER` line for claude in `test/provider-conformance.sh` is updated to the new argv, and the harness passes.
`docs/reference/events.md` is corrected: the sentence promising `usage: null` on a default install is no longer true.
userStories.notes: provider-conformance PASS — 5 providers covered with Claude argv including --output-format json; events PASS observed agent.turn usage input_tokens=1200, output_tokens=340, cost_usd=0.0421 from the structured result.

userStories.title: The agent loop is unaffected — output still reads as it did
userStories.description: The loop's contract with the provider's text output must survive. Prove it rather than assume it.
acceptanceCriteria: Completion detection still works: a turn emitting the completion promise still ends the loop with exit 0.
The turn's human-readable output still reaches the per-iteration log and `chief logs`, not raw JSON the operator has to decode.
`test/smoke.sh` passes — the end-to-end offline run is the regression net for exactly this.
A turn whose output is NOT valid JSON is handled without crashing the loop; the fallback is the pre-existing behaviour.
userStories.notes: bash test/provider-conformance.sh PASS — structured Claude result was humanized to the completion promise with no raw JSON in the operator log; the other provider doubles emitted invalid JSON and still completed with exit 0. bash test/smoke.sh PASS; bash test/ratelimit.sh PASS after preserving provider exit status and pinning the hermetic Claude fixture.

userStories.title: A provider that prints nothing usage-shaped still yields null, cleanly
userStories.description: The design rule holds: a guessed number is worse than a null, because a ledger cannot tell an invented figure from a measured one.
acceptanceCriteria: Providers with no usage output continue to emit `usage: null` — no zero-filling, no estimating from character counts.
The nullable, provider-dependent contract in `docs/reference/events.md` is preserved for every other provider.
`VERSION` is bumped and the README version string synced, because `engine/` changed — `test/version-bump.sh` and `test/doc-sync.sh` enforce both.
userStories.notes: bash test/events.sh PASS — providers with no usage-shaped output emitted usage:null on every event; docs preserve the nullable provider-dependent contract. VERSION 0.8.78 matches README **v0.8.78**; version-bump and doc-sync checks passed.
